attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack essay, giving his view on Flash Fill. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The draft keeps the 'I don't think' qualifier and the Flash Fill referent. It is a qualified belief about what systems could do in 2022, with no horizon. Phrasing it as Marcus's belief means it cannot be tested as a claim about the systems themselves.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats 'I don't think' as qualifying the comparison. It also notes that 'match' and 'pure deep learning' are undefined. Setting no empirical support or contradiction condition is fair to his words.

reviews.rationale: 'I don't think' is an epistemic qualifier, so this is a stated belief, not a firm assertion. 'Match it' and 'pure deep learning/big data system' are not defined. The packet has no evidence, and none could settle the qualified belief without changing its force. So the claim cannot be scored.
